Team,

We all make mistakes and unfortunately we didn’t catch the error on today’s email before we hit “send.”

Today we recognize the anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act, and the day it was signed by **President George H.W. Bush** , on July 26, 1990, not President Bill Clinton as our email incorrectly stated.

We apologize for the error. Nonetheless, we remember this important anniversary, and the diligence and hard work of organizers, activists, and leaders that led to this transformational piece of legislation.

[**Please, read our corrected email below, and then add your name to our petition.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/67107361/418613961/135770504?ms=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&refcode=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&source=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&utm_campaign=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=IYnE9McYs7F/u5Ot9NCG+2IHrhRm4XzIiZMdyOWat0SneOc0h1Ld6LSAQaDY+B5ojyrRejJkkCFOARyTmcya32XGUsstfvXVnWC7T3UMiuIDjdheFyuMDX5Ni6AhmR/rFlVHwHKTCjgGvcIktO3C4g==&refcode2=362c092b-082c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM5MjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzYyYzA5MmItMDgyYy1lZTExLWI4ZjAtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8kGuSk5LCr9abeelJwdc0n1b0sn1YlLIdrK-VWEzB6c=&emci=3e715d39-fe2b-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&emdi=362c092b-082c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&ceid=13528480)

\---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Sepi Shyne
Date: Jul 26, 2023
Subject: The first declaration of equality for people with disabilities.

Team,

The story of the Americans with Disabilities Act did not begin on July 26, 1990, when President George H.W. Bush put his pen on the monumental piece of legislation.

It began decades before when people with disabilities began challenging societal barriers and attitudes that had for too long excluded them, when parents began to fight against the segregation of their children, and when activists in the disabilities rights movement lobbied, protested, and fought for equal treatment, dignity, and opportunity.

**To them, we owe our deepest gratitude and respect.** Their organizing efforts led to our nation’s — and the world’s — first declaration of equality for people with disabilities; impacting the lives of millions of people and shifting our collective attitudes closer toward true inclusivity.

[**Remember this important milestone in our nation’s struggle for civil rights by adding your name to the petition calling on Congress to continue the work of the ADA and expand the rights of people with disabilities today. >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/67107362/418613965/135770504?ms=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&refcode=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&source=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&utm_campaign=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=IYnE9McYs7F/u5Ot9NCG+2IHrhRm4XzIiZMdyOWat0SneOc0h1Ld6LSAQaDY+B5ojyrRejJkkCFOARyTmcya32XGUsstfvXVnWC7T3UMiuIDjdheFyuMDX5Ni6AhmR/rFlVHwHKTCjgGvcIktO3C4g==&refcode2=362c092b-082c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&noskip=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM5MjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzYyYzA5MmItMDgyYy1lZTExLWI4ZjAtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8kGuSk5LCr9abeelJwdc0n1b0sn1YlLIdrK-VWEzB6c=&emci=3e715d39-fe2b-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&emdi=362c092b-082c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&ceid=13528480)

The Americans with Disabilities Act prohibits disability discrimination in the workplace and by state and local governments, ensures equal access to healthcare, social services, and transportation. It also provides standards for access to public spaces and affirms the inherent rights of people with disabilities to participate fully in every aspect of American life

But there is still so much more work that needs to be done for our nation to fully realize true inclusion and equality.

From housing accessibility and affordability, to disparities in health and education outcomes, we must keep moving the needle forward to protect the rights and dignity of people with disabilities.

I am calling on Congress to keep building on the work of disability rights activists to fund more accessible housing, increase funding for special education programs and programs to eliminate education disparities, and finally put an end to systemic discrimination faced by the disabled community.

[**Join me and add your name to urge Congress to renew our commitment to achieving the ADA’s full promise of advancing disability equity, dignity, access, and inclusion today. >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/67107366/418613972/135770504?ms=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&refcode=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&source=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&utm_campaign=em23_230726_kicker_adv_gq_act___TS_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=IYnE9McYs7F/u5Ot9NCG+2IHrhRm4XzIiZMdyOWat0SneOc0h1Ld6LSAQaDY+B5ojyrRejJkkCFOARyTmcya32XGUsstfvXVnWC7T3UMiuIDjdheFyuMDX5Ni6AhmR/rFlVHwHKTCjgGvcIktO3C4g==&refcode2=362c092b-082c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&noskip=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM5MjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzYyYzA5MmItMDgyYy1lZTExLWI4ZjAtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8kGuSk5LCr9abeelJwdc0n1b0sn1YlLIdrK-VWEzB6c=&emci=3e715d39-fe2b-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&emdi=362c092b-082c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&ceid=13528480)

clean_body: Team, We all make mistakes and unfortunately we didn’t catch the error on today’s email before we hit “send.” Today we recognize the anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act, and the day it was signed by President George H.W. Bush , on July 26, 1990, not President Bill Clinton as our email incorrectly stated. We apologize for the error. Nonetheless, we remember this important anniversary, and the diligence and hard work of organizers, activists, and leaders that led to this transformational piece of legislation. Thank you for your understanding, Team Shyne \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Sepi Shyne Date: Jul 26, 2023 Subject: The first declaration of equality for people with disabilities. Team, The story of the Americans with Disabilities Act did not begin on July 26, 1990, when President George H.W. Bush put his pen on the monumental piece of legislation. It began decades before when people with disabilities began challenging societal barriers and attitudes that had for too long excluded them, when parents began to fight against the segregation of their children, and when activists in the disabilities rights movement lobbied, protested, and fought for equal treatment, dignity, and opportunity. To them, we owe our deepest gratitude and respect. Their organizing efforts led to our nation’s — and the world’s — first declaration of equality for people with disabilities; impacting the lives of millions of people and shifting our collective attitudes closer toward true inclusivity. The Americans with Disabilities Act prohibits disability discrimination in the workplace and by state and local governments, ensures equal access to healthcare, social services, and transportation. It also provides standards for access to public spaces and affirms the inherent rights of people with disabilities to participate fully in every aspect of American life But there is still so much more work that needs to be done for our nation to fully realize true inclusion and equality. From housing accessibility and affordability, to disparities in health and education outcomes, we must keep moving the needle forward to protect the rights and dignity of people with disabilities. I am calling on Congress to keep building on the work of disability rights activists to fund more accessible housing, increase funding for special education programs and programs to eliminate education disparities, and finally put an end to systemic discrimination faced by the disabled community. With gratitude, Sepi Shyne #WomanLifeFreedom Mayor Sepi Shyne has taken on WeHo's biggest issues and delivered results. From raising the minimum wage to the highest in the nation to significantly reducing homelessness – she's running for Congress to fight for all of us. As the first out Iranian LGBTQ+ woman elected anywhere in the world, Sepi is committed to making the American dream a reality for everyone: For immigrants, the LGBTQ+ community, women, and anyone trying to make ends meet. name: Tina Smith
subject: Equality for everyone
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tina Smith for Minnesota
body:
The ADA made huge strides to level the playing field for people with disabilities across the country. |
#
Hi folks — Today marks the 33rd anniversary of the _Americans with Disabilities Act_. This ground-breaking legislation, signed into law by President George H.W. Bush, made huge strides to level the playing field for people with disabilities across the country. Workplaces, schools, playgrounds, shopping malls, and so many other places around our country have become more welcoming and inclusive to people with disabilities, both visible and invisible. **But there is more to be done, and I’m working in the Senate to make our country more fair and inclusive for everyone.** I’ve worked with colleagues, both Democrats and Republicans, to improve access to healthcare for veterans with disabilities and for those seeking behavioral health treatment. I also proudly supported President Biden’s Bipartisan Infrastructure Deal, which provides critical investments to make our transit systems more accessible for everyone. **[On this anniversary, I am recommitting myself to protecting and expanding civil rights for people with disabilities — and I hope you’ll join my pledge to support and expand the _ADA_ for years to come.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/67108139/418617000/-1694076152?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=AU_TSM_EG_GEN_PET_AC60_20230726_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTU1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzllZjFlOS0wYzJjLWVlMTEtYjhmMC0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ge-9pzZQwybNRo6VVqoFY1no4WJkqO3i9BwRhp4UDfk=&emci=6a9ef1e9-0c2c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&emdi=839ef1e9-0c2c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&ceid=6227932)** | [SIGN ON](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/67108140/418617001/-1694076152?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=AU_TSM_EG_GEN_PET_AC60_20230726_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTU1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzllZjFlOS0wYzJjLWVlMTEtYjhmMC0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ge-9pzZQwybNRo6VVqoFY1no4WJkqO3i9BwRhp4UDfk=&emci=6a9ef1e9-0c2c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&emdi=839ef1e9-0c2c-ee11-b8f0-00224832eb73&ceid=6227932)

Friend,

_Politico_ reported this week that House Republicans are preparing to pass hard-right spending bills in advance of the government funding deadline — bills that they know _cannot_ pass the Senate.

They’re trying to stuff basic government funding legislation with extreme measures such as denying abortion access to veterans, cutting federal nutrition programs, defunding organizations that support LGBTQ Americans, and barring DREAMers from federal employment.

**House Republicans are once again playing dangerous political games that could escalate into a government shutdown. And as someone who represents a district with over 30,000 federal workers, Jennifer is outraged.**

Too often in our political discourse, we forget the value of our federal workers — the exact people who stand to lose when Republicans force unnecessary government shutdowns. Federal workers uphold our national security, transportation, essential services, and landmarks. They are what makes our country run effectively.

But time and time again, the far right demonizes federal workers and uses them as political pawns. In fact, when Jennifer first entered Congress, we were in the middle of a government shutdown caused by a Donald Trump temper tantrum. Millions of workers (including many in VA-10) were furloughed without pay for weeks, and real economic hardship was felt among them.

Jennifer will _always_ use her platform and her voice to protect federal workers, and as we gear up for a big fight in the weeks ahead, she needs the resources to take on Republican lies and make sure that far-right proposals do not become law.

clean_body: Jennifer stands ready to fight them. = = = = Friend, Politico reported this week that House Republicans are preparing to pass hard-right spending bills in advance of the government funding deadline — bills that they know cannot pass the Senate. They’re trying to stuff basic government funding legislation with extreme measures such as denying abortion access to veterans, cutting federal nutrition programs, defunding organizations that support LGBTQ Americans, and barring DREAMers from federal employment. House Republicans are once again playing dangerous political games that could escalate into a government shutdown. And as someone who represents a district with over 30,000 federal workers, Jennifer is outraged. Too often in our political discourse, we forget the value of our federal workers — the exact people who stand to lose when Republicans force unnecessary government shutdowns. Federal workers uphold our national security, transportation, essential services, and landmarks. They are what makes our country run effectively. But time and time again, the far right demonizes federal workers and uses them as political pawns. In fact, when Jennifer first entered Congress, we were in the middle of a government shutdown caused by a Donald Trump temper tantrum. Millions of workers (including many in VA-10) were furloughed without pay for weeks, and real economic hardship was felt among them.
